All three solutions compute the same quantity, ∫₀^{2π}|f′(θ)|dθ = 4π, and none of them reaches the correct perimeter. The correct answer appears to be 8π/3 + 2√3, which none of them give.

Write f(θ) = ((1+e^{iθ})³ − 1)/3. Then f′(θ) = i e^{iθ}(1+e^{iθ})², so |f′(θ)| = 2 + 2cos θ. Integrating over the full parameter range gives 4π, which is the length of the whole parametrized curve.

That curve is not simple, so 4π is not the perimeter of the region it encloses. Put 1+e^{iθ} = 2cos(θ/2)e^{iθ/2}, so (f+1/3)·3 = 8cos³(θ/2)e^{3iθ/2}. In polar form with ψ = 3θ/2, this curve is r = 8cos³(ψ/3) for ψ in (−3π/2, 3π/2).

Points at angles ψ and ψ − 2π coincide only when ψ = π. That is a self-intersection at f = −2/3. Beyond it, the portions with |ψ| in (π, 3π/2) form a small inner loop that ends at the cusp f = −1/3.

The outer boundary is therefore only the portion with θ in [−2π/3, 2π/3]. Its length is

∫ (2 + 2cos θ) dθ = 2[θ + sin θ] from −2π/3 to 2π/3 = 8π/3 + 2√3.

Since all three solutions give 4π, none is correct. Solution 1 is the only one to check the curve's structure, although it wrongly concludes the curve is simple. I pick it as the closest.

CHOICE: 1
